name: Notion, Cards
description: Records from any Notion database as a grid of bordered cards. Choose up to five columns to show on each card, each at its own size, with or without its name; how a column is drawn follows its Notion type. Filter by up to three column conditions, sort by any column, group under headings, cap the count. Supports several Notion accounts. Requires the Notion Core plugin.

cell_options.name: data_source
cell_options.label: Database
cell_options.help: Every database your Notion accounts can see, prefixed by account name when more than one is configured. Picking one also selects that account: a Notion database belongs to exactly one workspace, so there is nothing else to choose. Nothing listed? Open the database in Notion, then ••• → Connections → add your integration.

cell_options.name: columns
cell_options.label: Columns
cell_options.help: Cards per row. Rows follow from this and the record limit. Small cells cap it: 1 at xs, 2 at sm, 4 at md.

cell_options.name: limit
cell_options.label: Max records shown
cell_options.help: Every card gets an equal share of the cell, so more records means smaller cards.

cell_options.name: field_gap
cell_options.label: Space between properties
cell_options.help: Extra white space between one property and the next on every card, on top of the small gap always there. 0 keeps them tight; 5 is airy. Measured in em, so it scales with the cell's text.

cell_options.name: prop1
cell_options.label: Property 1
cell_options.help: Type a Notion column name exactly (the Notion Core admin page's Inspect columns link lists them). How it is drawn follows its type: a checkbox as a checkbox, a select or status as badges, a date as a date, a rollup that gathers several values as one line per value, anything else as text. Leave every property blank to show just the title column. The two options below only apply once this is set.

cell_options.name: prop1_lines
cell_options.label: Property 1 max lines
cell_options.help: For text. 1 keeps it to one line, cut with an ellipsis; more lets it wrap, up to that many lines. A rollup that gathers several values always lists them one per line, whatever this is set to.

cell_options.name: prop2
cell_options.label: Property 2
cell_options.help: Blank = not shown. The two options below only apply once Property 2 is set.

cell_options.name: group_prop
cell_options.label: Group by column (blank = no grouping)
cell_options.help: Type a Notion column name exactly. Cards collect under a heading per value, in the order they are sorted; cards with nothing in the column go last under 'No <column>'. A column with several values files the card under the first.

cell_options.name: filter_prop
cell_options.label: Filter 1: column (blank = no filter)
cell_options.help: Type a Notion column name exactly. The condition and value below only apply once this is set. Every filter that names a column must hold.

choices.label: is at least / is on or after
is at most / is on or before

cell_options.name: filter_value
cell_options.label: Filter 1: value
cell_options.help: Matched case-insensitively. For 'is one of', a comma-separated list: This Week, Next Week. For a date column, type a date (2026-09-30), a month (2026-09) or the word 'today'. For a checkbox, 'yes' or 'no'. Not used by 'is empty' / 'is not empty'.

cell_options.name: filter2_prop
cell_options.label: Filter 2: column (blank = unused)
cell_options.help: A further condition, combined with the others: a record must satisfy all of them.

choices.label: is at least / is on or after
is at most / is on or before

cell_options.name: filter3_prop
cell_options.label: Filter 3: column (blank = unused)
cell_options.help: A further condition, combined with the others: a record must satisfy all of them.

choices.label: is at least / is on or after
is at most / is on or before

cell_options.name: sort_prop
cell_options.label: Sort by column (blank = Notion's order)
cell_options.help: Type a Notion column name exactly. Records with nothing in the column go last.

cell_options.name: sort2_prop
cell_options.label: Then sort by column (blank = none)
cell_options.help: Breaks ties in the first sort. Type a Notion column name exactly.

cell_options.name: filter_person
cell_options.label: Only show items for
cell_options.help: Leave blank to show everything. Type 'me' for whoever owns the Notion token (exact, and filtered by Notion itself), or a person's name as it appears in Notion.

cell_options.name: filter_columns
cell_options.label: Filter columns (blank = the people column)
cell_options.help: Comma-separated Notion column names. A row is kept if ANY of them matches. Blank uses the auto-detected people column. Only used when 'Only show items for' is set.
